newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Arafat arrives in Sri Lanka for short visit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat arrives in Sri Lanka for short visit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, currently embroiled in a major diplomatic row with Israel, arrived in Sri Lanka on Monday on a short visit during which he will meet President Chandrika Kumaratunga.

Arafat, whose arrival from Islamabad was delayed by nearly two and a half hours, was received by Sri Lankan foreign minister Lakshman Kadirgamar and other officials at the Bandaranaike International Airport, 23 km (14 miles) from Colombo.
He was later flown into Colombo aboard an air force helicopter.
Security was tight in Colombo as his helicopter landed at the military headquarters grounds overlooking the Galle Face promenade near the Presidential secretariat.
Naval ships could be seen patrolling the sea off Galle Face.

The Palestinian president is scheduled to call on Sri Lankan Prime Minister Sirima Bandaranaike and address a public meeting on Monday. He will later be the guest at an official banquet hosted by Kumaratunga.
Arafat lambasted Tel Aviv on Sunday for its plan to build a new settlement in Arab east Jerusalem.
He told an Islamic summit in Islamabad that Israeli policies were bringing the Middle East peace process to a dead-end.

"We are surprised by the Israeli decision to isolate and Judaise Jerusalem, constructing new settlements not only inside it but outside it," Arafat told a one-day summit of the 54-member Organisation of the Islamic Conference.

Israeli-Palestinian tension has been high since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers last Tuesday to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a new Jewish settlement in territory occupied by Israel.
Arafat leaves for the Bangladeshi capital Dhaka on Tuesday.
